name: package_integrity
description: The toolkit's declared trust anchor, under test on whichever distro the endpoint is. The ssh CLIENT is backdoored in place and made SUID — real tradecraft, since a trojaned ssh harvests every credential the host uses to reach anywhere else. adjudicate.py calls a package-owned-but-modified binary Likely True Positive regardless of finding type, and the correlator promotes it to a DEFINITIVE dimension: the strongest verdict the Linux side reaches, because a package manager does not let installed files drift from their recorded contents. Run this on EVERY distro — pkg_modified branches to debsums, rpm -Vf, pacman -Qkk and apk audit, and a branch that never executes is a trust anchor nobody has weighed. The apk branch was missing entirely until Alpine was added here.

expect.id: the tampered binary is FLAGGED (SUID outside the baseline)
the package manager resolves OWNERSHIP of the binary
the package manager reports the file as MODIFIED — the trust anchor fires
adjudication rates a tampered packaged binary a true positive
